walkthroughs.body_html:
Concentration, temperature, surface area and catalysts all affect rate.

More frequent or more energetic collisions -> faster rate.

Exothermic reactions release energy (burning, neutralisation).

Endothermic reactions take energy in (thermal decomposition, photosynthesis).

Energy change = products - reactants.

Measure: mass change, gas volume or how long until a cross is hidden.

Repeat for reliability; calculate mean rate.

options: more catalyst forms
particles collide more often and with more energy
activation energy falls
volume decreases
thermal decomposition of CaCO3
dissolving NH4NO3
combustion of methane
photosynthesis

mcqs.q: How does a catalyst speed up a reaction?
options: A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.
A catalyst lowers the activation energy of the original reaction pathway.
It provides an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy.
Higher temperature increases the concentration of the reactants.

mcqs.q: In an exothermic reaction, what happens energetically with the bonds?
options: Energy released forming new bonds exceeds energy absorbed breaking existing bonds.
Higher temperature increases the concentration of the reactants.
The reactants get colder because they lose mass as energy.
Bond breaking releases energy and bond making absorbs energy.

mcqs.q: Why does increasing temperature increase the rate of reaction significantly?
options: A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.
Higher temperature increases the concentration of the reactants.
Particles collide much more frequently at higher temperature, which is the main reason for the rate increase.
Mainly because a much larger fraction of collisions have energy at least equal to the activation energy; collision frequency increases only slightly.
